subject: Clarify IP handback, go-live constraints, and training opt-in
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@stratusworks.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; procurement@stratusworks.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on IP assignment & training clause (Order Form)

Hi Laura / Ben / Karthik —

Thanks again for the redlines. Legal at StratusWorks ran a focused review overnight and a few items came up that we need clarified before procurement completes the PO and we route for signatures:  

1) Output ownership: your latest MSA language appears to assign output to StratusWorks but the Order Form has an exception for model-derived productization. Can you confirm whether the proposal is (A) full assignment of generated output to us, or (B) a perpetual, transferable license? We need this explicitly for our IP team.

2) Training / feedback: the draft grant a feedback license to Redwood to use customer data for model training. StratusWorks must ensure data used for training will be either (i) anonymized & aggregated, or (ii) only with explicit opt-in per dataset. Please propose an operational approach and retention window.

3) Go-live constraints & staging handback: our compliance team insisted on a 90-day escrow/holding period for telemetry and a staging handback step before production cutover. Any objections? What telemetry fields do you need and how long must logs be retained for operational SLOs?

Attached is a short evidence checklist our procurement team needs (SOC 2 snapshot, KMS attestation). We appreciate a short call if easier.  

Best,
Maya Patel
Sr. Counsel, StratusWorks
[Attachment: Stratus-evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@stratusworks.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on IP assignment & training clause (Order Form)

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. I'll address each item below and propose concrete language for legal to react to. Happy to hop on a 30-min call today if that helps.

1) Output ownership: Our recommended position is to keep the MSA as an assignment-of-output model for customer-generated content (so StratusWorks would own output it submits and receives). For productization (i.e., building a model derived from StratusWorks data and selling it), Redwood requests a limited, non-exclusive license back to Redwood for internal model improvement unless the customer opts-out. Suggested redline: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Output. Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Customer Output solely to improve Redwood services unless Customer expressly opts out in writing."

2) Training / feedback: We can operationalize opt-in per dataset. Default: no training unless Customer opts-in. If Customer opts-in, Redwood will only use data after automated anonymization and aggregation. Retention window for customer telemetry used in model research: 90 days for raw logs; aggregated/anonymized artifacts retained up to 24 months for model evaluation. We'll add explicit KMS/HSM controls and deletion attestations in the evidence pack.

3) Go-live constraints & staging handback: No objection to a staging handback step. Proposed flow: (a) initial staging period (30 days) with telemetry collection for SLO tuning; (b) handback sign-off from StratusWorks CS and Security; (c) production cutover. Telemetry fields needed: request timestamp, model_id, route, token-latency, partial error codes, and anonymized prompt/trace identifiers (not full user content). Raw telemetry retained 90 days as above; full request payloads are deleted unless retained under a signed opt-in for training.

I'm attaching our latest redlines with the suggested language inline. I'll loop in legal if we want to trade changes in redline form.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Contracts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_redlines_v2.docx (document)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T12:16:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on IP assignment & training clause (Order Form)

Laura / Karthik — quick note before we respond back to Maya:

I agree with the track Laura proposed. A couple tactical concessions to speed procurement:
- Offer StratusWorks an option box on the Order Form: "Training Opt-in: Yes / No" that controls whether data can be used for model training. Default = No.
- For productization license, convert "non-transferable" to "non-exclusive, revocable for opt-out customers" so they feel more comfortable — we can retain rights for internal model improvement but surface an audit process.
- Provide a signed attestation (one-off PDF) that raw request payloads will be removed within 90 days unless opted-in. That should clear procurement checklists.

If Karthik and Legal are happy, I'll propose we send a compromise summary back to Maya and include a DocuSign link for the Order Form checkbox and the attestation.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
